Stem cells used in HSCT may be obtained from one of three 
sources: a donor (related or unrelated), a genetically identical 
twin, or the individual who will be undergoing HSCT. Donor
transplantation is referred to as allogeneic HSCT. If the donor
is a genetically identical twin, it is referred to as syngeneic 
HSCT. When patients donate their own stem cells, the proce-
dure is referred to as autologous HSCT. Th ose patients under-
going an allogeneic HSCT are at highest risk for developing 
transplant-related morbidity and mortality due to complica-
tions secondary to graft-versus-host disease.

cells are used, or by a procedure called apheresis if peripheral 
stem cells are used) from the donor or the patient. After a cer-
tain period of time, the patient undergoes high-dose chemo-
therapy and/or total body irradiation (TBI), which is referred
